And my success is only by God; upon Him I rely and to Him I turn in repentance.

So the correct position on this question, God willing, is to say: There is no doubt that the sin itself does not turn into a good deed, and a good deed is only an existential matter that calls for a reward. For this reason, the one who abandons what is forbidden is rewarded only for restraining his soul and withholding it from committing what is forbidden, and that restraint and withholding is an existential matter, and it is the object of the reward.

As for the one whose mind never brought up the sin at all and who never entertained it, how could he be rewarded for abandoning it? If such a person were rewarded for abandoning this sin, he would be rewarded for abandoning the sins of the whole world which never occurred to his mind, and that would exceed his good deeds without number, for abandonment accompanies him, and what is abandoned is not limited or bounded. Would he be rewarded for all of that? This is not even conceivable.

And if a good deed must be an existential matter, then the penitent from the sins he committed has accompanied each of them with regret for it, restraint of his soul from it, and resolve to never return to it. These are good deeds without doubt, and repentance has erased the trace of the sin and left behind this regret and resolve, and this is a good deed which has replaced that evil deed with a good deed.

This is the meaning of the saying of some exegetes: "He makes the repentance take the place of the evil deed, and the good deed is with the repentance."

So if every evil deed of his has been repented of, then his repentance from it is a good deed which has taken its place. This is the meaning of substitution, not that the evil deed itself turns into a good deed.

Some exegetes said regarding this verse: "He gives them, through regret for every evil they committed, a good deed." According to this, by God's praise the difficulty has gone away, the correct view has become clear, and it has become evident that each of the two groups did not depart from the requirement of knowledge and proof.

As for the hadith of Abu Dhar, although the substitution in it concerns the persistent sinner who was punished for his evil deeds, it indicates by way of a stronger inference that substitution occurs for the penitent who has ceased and regrets his evil deeds. For the sins for which the persistent one was punished, when their trace was removed by the punishment, remained as though they had never been. So God gives him, in place of each of them, a good deed, because what befell him on the Day of Resurrection of excessive regret for them, together with the punishment, necessitated the removal of their trace and their substitution with good deeds. For regret was not at a time when it would benefit him, so when he was punished for them and their trace was removed, God replaced them for him with good deeds.

So the removal of their trace through sincere repentance is greater than the removal of their trace through punishment. Therefore, if they are replaced with good deeds after their removal through punishment, then their replacement with good deeds after their removal through repentance is more fitting and more deserving. And the effect of repentance in this erasure and substitution is stronger than the effect of punishment, because repentance is a voluntary act which the servant performs willingly, out of love for God and fear of Him.

As for punishment, its expiation is of the same kind as the expiation through calamities that befall him without his choice, rather by the act of God. And there is no doubt that the effect of voluntary acts which God loves and is pleased with in erasing sins is greater than the effect of calamities that reach him without his choice.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 25, verse 68–70 (part 1 of 3):

It is related in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from him (ﷺ) that he was asked: "Which sin is the greatest in the sight of Allah?" He said: "That you set up a rival (nidd) to Allah while He created you." It was said: "Then what?" He said: "That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you." It was said: "Then what?" He said: "That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour." Then Allah the Exalted revealed its confirmation:
﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except in truth, and do not commit adultery﴾ [al-Furqan: 68].

And since the corruption of fornication (zina) is among the greatest of corruptions, and it is contrary to the welfare of the order of the world in preserving lineages, protecting chastity, safeguarding sanctities, and averting what causes the greatest enmity and hatred among people, through each of them corrupting the wife, daughter, sister and mother of the other, and in that is the ruin of the world, it follows the corruption of killing in gravity. For this reason Allah the Glorified joined it with it in His Book, and His Messenger (ﷺ) in his Sunnah, as has preceded.

Imam Ahmad said: "I know of nothing, after killing a soul, greater than fornication."

Allah the Glorified has emphasised its prohibition by His saying:
﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except in truth, and do not commit adultery; and whoever does that will meet a penalty. The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation — except one who repents﴾ [al-Furqan: 68–70].

So He joined fornication with shirk and the killing of a soul, and made the recompense for that abiding in a doubled punishment, so long as the servant does not remove the cause of that by repentance, faith and righteous action.

[The destruction of the soul is the punishment of the most heinous kinds of crimes]
Consider how the destruction of souls came in opposition to the greatest of the major sins, the most harmful and the most corrupting to the world: namely original and acquired disbelief (kufr), killing, and adultery of the married person (zina al-muhsan). When the intelligent person reflects on the corruption of existence, he sees it from these three directions. These are the three which "the Prophet (ﷺ) answered 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud with, when he said to him: O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest? He said: That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you. He said: I said: Then what? He said: That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you. He said: I said: Then what? He said: That you commit adultery with the wife of your neighbour." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the confirmation of that: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except in truth, and do not commit adultery﴾ [al-Furqan: 68], and so on.

(Section: The roots of all sins, great and small, are three)
Attachment of the heart to other than Allah, and obedience to the irascible faculty (al-quwwa al-ghadabiyya) and the appetitive faculty (al-quwwa al-shahwaniyya); and these are shirk, injustice (zulm), and indecencies (fawahish).

The ultimate of attachment to other than Allah is shirk, and that another god be invoked besides Him. The ultimate of obedience to the irascible faculty is killing, and the ultimate of the appetitive faculty is zina. For this reason Allah the Glorified combined the three in His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except in truth, and do not commit adultery﴾.

These three draw one another on: shirk calls to injustice and indecencies, just as sincerity (ikhlas) and tawhid turn them away from their owner. Allah says: ﴿Thus, that We might avert from him evil and indecency; indeed, he is of Our sincere servants﴾ [Yusuf: 24]. So "evil" is passionate love (ishq), and "indecency" is zina. Likewise injustice calls to shirk and indecency, for shirk is the greatest injustice, just as the greatest justice is tawhid.

Justice is the companion of tawhid, and injustice is the companion of shirk; for this reason Allah combines them. As for the first, it is in His saying: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those of knowledge, standing in justice﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18]. As for the second, it is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, shirk is a great injustice﴾ [Luqman: 13].

Indecency calls to shirk and injustice, especially when its desire is strong and it is not attained except through some kind of injustice, and through seeking help from sorcery and the devil.

Allah has combined zina and shirk in His saying: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist; and that has been made unlawful to the believers﴾ [al-Nur: 3].

So these three drag one another along and command one another. For this reason, whenever the heart is weaker in tawhid and greater in shirk, it is more prone to indecency, and more attached to images (suwar) and in love with them.

[Among the wisdom of Allah is the legislation of the hudud]
It was part of His wisdom and mercy, the Glorified, that He legislated punishments for the crimes committed among people against one another, against heads, bodies, honour and property, such as killing, wounding, slander (qadhf) and theft. He perfected in the utmost perfection the forms of deterrence that restrain these crimes, and legislated them in the most complete manner, containing the benefit of deterrence and restraint, while not exceeding what the offender deserves of deterrence. Thus He did not legislate for lying the cutting of the tongue, nor for adultery castration, nor for theft the annihilation of the soul.

Rather, He legislated for them in this what is required by His names and attributes: His wisdom, mercy, kindness, benevolence and justice, so that calamities may vanish, and desires to wrong and transgress may be cut off, and every person may be content with what his Owner and Creator has given him, so that he does not covet to seize the right of another.

[Crimes vary, so punishments vary]
It is known that these four crimes have distinct levels in fewness and multiplicity, and different degrees in severity of harm and lightness of it, just as all other sins vary in greatness and smallness and what lies between.

It is known that the forbidden glance cannot be equated in punishment with the punishment of one who commits fornication, nor a scratch with a wood splinter with a strike of the sword, nor light verbal abuse with slander by zina and the defaming of lineages; nor the theft of a morsel or a fils with the theft of a large, great amount of property. Since the levels of crimes differ, there must be a difference in the levels of punishments. It is known that if people were left to their own intellects to determine this and to arrange each punishment according to what suits its crime in kind, attribute and measure, opinions would take them every which way, paths would divide them in every direction, disagreement would grow great, and the matter would become grave. So the Most Merciful of the merciful and the Most Wise of the judges spared them that burden, removed from them its hardship, and by His wisdom, knowledge and mercy took charge of its determination in kind and measure, and arranged for each crime the punishment that suits it and befits it as a deterrent. Then, in the breadth of His mercy and generosity, He went so far as to make those punishments expiations (kaffarat) for their people and a purification that removes from them the blame for the crimes when they come before Him, especially if after them there is sincere repentance (tawba nasuh) and turning back. So He showed them mercy through these punishments in kinds of mercy in this world and the Hereafter, and He made these punishments revolve around six principles: killing, cutting, flogging, exile, fining of property, and discretionary punishment (ta'zir).

[Killing and its justification]
As for killing, He made it the punishment for the greatest crimes, such as crimes against souls; so its punishment is of its own kind. And as for crime against the religion by reviling it and apostasy from it, this crime is more deserving of killing, and of restraining the criminal's aggression against Him, than any other punishment; for his survival among His servants is a corruption for them, and no good is hoped for in his survival, nor any benefit. So if he restrains his evil, holds back his tongue, withholds his harm, and accepts humiliation and abasement, the running of the rulings of Allah and His Messenger upon him, and payment of the jizya, then his survival among the Muslims does no harm to them; and the world is a provision and enjoyment for a time. He also made it the punishment for crime against forbidden private parts, because of the great corruptions in it, the mixing of lineages, and general corruption.

(Section)
Know that Allah the Glorified created His believing servants, and created everything for their sake, as He said: ﴿Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, and has completed upon you His favours, apparent and hidden?﴾ [Luqman: 20].

And He honoured them and preferred them over many of those He created, so He said: ﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam and carried them on land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference﴾ [al-Isra: 70]. And He said to their righteous and chosen ones: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of 'Imran over the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 33].

And Allah said to Musa: ﴿And I have chosen you for Myself﴾ [Ta-Ha: 41]. And He took two of them as intimate friends (khalilayn), and intimacy (khulla) is the highest degree of love.

It has come in some reports: Allah the Exalted says: "Son of Adam, I created you for Myself, and I created everything for you. So by My right over you, do not occupy yourself with what I created for you in a way that distracts you from that for which I created you."

And in another report Allah the Exalted says: "Son of Adam, I created you for Myself, so do not play; and I have guaranteed your provision, so do not tire yourself. Son of Adam, seek Me and you will find Me; for if you find Me you have found everything, and if you miss Me you have missed everything, and I am more beloved to you than everything."

So Allah the Glorified created His servants for Himself; and for this reason He bought from them their selves, and this is a contract He did not make with the creation of others, as He informed through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ), so that they might hand over to Him the souls He created for Himself.

This purchase is evidence that they are beloved to Him, chosen by Him, and pleasing in His sight.

The worth of a commodity is known by the exalted rank of its buyer and the measure of its price. This is when its worth in itself is unknown; but when the commodity's worth is known, its buyer is known, and the price offered for it is known, its status and rank in existence is known. The commodity is you; Allah is the Buyer; the price is His Paradise and gazing upon His Face and hearing His speech in the abode of security and peace.

Allah the Glorified chooses for Himself only the most precious things, the most noble, and the greatest in value. And when He has chosen the servant for Himself and been pleased with him for His knowledge and love, built him a house in His vicinity and nearness, and made His angels his servants, running about in his interests in his waking and his sleep, his life and his death; then the servant runs away from his master and owner, turning away from his pleasure; and that does not suffice him, until he defects and makes peace with his enemy and allies himself with him instead of Him, and becomes one of his soldiers, preferring the pleasure of the enemy over the pleasure of his Lord and Owner. Then he has sold his self — which his God and Owner bought from him, making its price His Paradise and gazing upon His Face — to his enemy and the most hateful of His creatures to Him, and exchanged His anger for His pleasure, His curse for His mercy and His love.

So what hatred has this deceived person left unencountered from his Lord?

Allah says: ﴿And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblis. He was of the jinn and departed from the command of his Lord. Then would you take him and his descendants as allies other than Me while they are an enemy to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Kahf: 50].

So reflect on what lies beneath this rebuke, and what is folded within this address of the wickedness of this servant, and what he is exposed to of hatred, disgrace and humiliation; and on [the Lord's] seeking his favour, asking him to make amends, and calling him back to return to his true ally and master, who is more deserving of him. When he returns to Him and repents to Him, he is like one whose beloved has been captured by an enemy who took hold of him and came between him and his beloved; then that beloved fled from them and came willingly and obediently to his lover, until he laid his head upon the threshold of his door. The lover came out of his house and found his beloved laying his head on the threshold of his door, placing his cheek and chin upon it. How then would his Lord rejoice? And to Allah belongs the highest likeness.

And it suffices in this parable which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck for whoever Allah has opened the eye of his heart, so that he perceives what lies within it and what it contains, and knows that it is not a figure of speech, nor exaggeration, nor imagination; but a word protected in its structure, its knowledge, its intent and its deed, every word of it in its place, its rank and its station, neither exceeding it nor falling short of it.

What further establishes this meaning is that the Lord's love for His servant preceded the servant's love for Him, the Glorified. For were it not for Allah's love for him, He would not have placed His love in his heart. When He loved him, He inspired him with His love and gave him preference with it; then when the servant loved Him, He rewarded that love with a greater love, for whoever draws near to Him a span, He draws near to him a cubit; whoever draws near to Him a cubit, He draws near to him a fathom; and whoever comes to Him walking, He comes to him running.

This is evidence that Allah's love for the servant whom He loves is above the servant's love for Him.

So when this beloved exposes himself to the displeasure of his Beloved, he is like the beloved who fled from his lover and preferred another over him; then when he returns to him, turns towards him and abandons the other, how would his lover not rejoice in him with the greatest and most complete joy? The witness is the strongest witness, supported by innate nature (fitra) and reason. Even if the Truthful and Believed one had not informed of this great matter, there would still be in innate nature and reason what bears witness to it. When the revealed Law is combined with the perfecting innate nature and with sound, illuminated reason, that is the thing beyond which there is no further end; and that is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of Infinite Bounty.

(Section)
Whenever the servant wishes to witness this in himself, let him look at the joy he finds after sincere repentance, and the gladness and pleasure that come to him; and the reward is of the same kind as the deed.

So when he repents to Allah and Allah rejoices at his repentance, He follows it with a great joy. Here is a subtlety few grasp except a jurist in this matter: every penitent must, at the outset of his repentance, experience a squeezing and pressure in his heart of distress, grief, constriction or sorrow; even if it is nothing but his pain at parting from his beloved, so his heart is pressed by that and constricted, and his breast tightens. Most people turn back from repentance and fall on their heads because of this trial.

The discerning and successful knower understands that the joy, gladness and pleasure that arise after repentance are in proportion to this squeezing: the stronger and more intense it is, the more complete and perfect the joy and pleasure will be. And there are many reasons for this, among them: that this squeezing and constriction is a sign of the life of his heart and the strength of his readiness; for if his heart were dead and his readiness weak, this would not have happened to him...

Also, Satan is a thief of faith, and a thief only targets a place that is populated and inhabited. As for a ruined place from which he expects to gain nothing, he does not target it. So when satanic opposition and pressure intensify, this indicates that there is in the heart some good that Satan is very eager to remove.

Also, the strength of an opposing force indicates the strength of what opposes it. Such a person is either a leader in goodness or a leader in evil. Strong, unyielding souls, if they are good, excel in goodness, and if they are wicked, they excel in wickedness.

Also, in proportion to his acceptance of this obstacle and his patience with it, there results for him certainty, steadfastness, and resolve, which necessitate an increase in his expansion of heart and tranquility. Also, the greater the sought-after goal, the more obstacles and barriers stand in its way. This is the way of Allah with His creation.

Consider Paradise, its greatness, and the barriers and obstructions that stand between a person and it, to the point that only one man out of every thousand goes to it. Consider love of Allah, devotion to Him, turning to Him, dedicating oneself to Him alone, intimacy with Him, and taking Him as a protector, trustee, sufficient one, and reckoner. Can a servant acquire anything more noble than this?

Consider the obstacles and barriers that stand between a person and Him, to the point that every group has become attached to what they are attached to instead of Him: among the seekers are those who stop at their deeds, those who stop at their knowledge, those who stop at their spiritual states, those who stop at their spiritual taste, their collectedness, and their share from their Lord, while the One sought is beyond all of that.

The point is that this matter achieved through repentance, since it is among the greatest and most important affairs, has had obstacles and trials set against it, so that the truthful may be distinguished from the liar, trial may occur, testing may take place, and those who are fit may be distinguished from those who are not. Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. Do people think that they will be left to say "We believe" and will not be tested? And We had certainly tested those before them, and Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful, and He will surely make evident the liars.﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 1-3]. And He says: ﴿That He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [Al-Mulk: 2]. But if he is patient with this pressure for a little while, it will lead him to gardens of intimacy and paradises of expansion of heart. If he is not patient with it, he will turn back on his face. Allah is the Granter of success; there is no god but Him, and there is no lord besides Him.

The point is that this joy from Allah at the repentance of His servant, although its like is not found in any other act of obedience, is evidence of the great value and virtue of repentance before Allah, and that worshipping Him through it is among the most noble forms of worship. This shows that the one who repents returns more perfect than he was before. This is some of what has been cited as evidence for this view.

As for the group who said: he does not return to what he was, but rather his state must decline, they argued that sin necessarily brings estrangement, the loss of love, and a decline in servanthood, without doubt.

The servant who spends his times in obedience to his Master is not like the servant who neglects his duties toward Him, and this cannot be denied or contested. So when he repents to his Lord and returns to Him, his repentance results in the blessing of being forgiven for his sin and pardoned for it. But as for the station of nearness and love, far be it that he returns to it.

They said: Moreover, during the time he was occupied with disobedience, he missed the journey to Allah. So if he had remained in his place, he would still have missed progress. How much more so when, during the time of sin, his journey was backward upon backward?

So if he repents and turns his journey forward again, he needs a new journey and the covering of a distance until he reaches the position he fell behind from.

They said: We do not deny that he may perform acts of obedience and deeds that bring him to his former rank. We only deny that by sincere repentance alone he returns to his rank and state, and this does not happen. For by repentance he has turned his face toward the path, and he will not reach the place he returned from except by a renewed journey that brings him there. We do not deny that after repentance the servant performs great deeds that he would not have performed before the sin, which earn him advancement.

They said: Moreover, if he returned to the state he was in, or to a higher one, he would be equal to the one who persistently obeys, or in better condition than him. How can this be, when where is the journey of the one who obeys during the time the other was occupied with disobedience? How can two men meet, one traveling east and the other west? If one of them returns to the other's path while the other is still diligent on his journey, the one who went ahead will remain ahead as long as no slackness or lethargy befalls him. This cannot be denied or refuted.

They said: Moreover, the sickness of the heart through sins is like the sickness of the body through illnesses, and repentance is like taking medicine. When the sick person takes medicine and recovers, his strength does not return to him as it was before the illness, or if it does, it returns after some time.

They said: Moreover, during the time of treating through repentance, he is occupied with mending himself and treating it, while during the time of sin he is occupied with its desires. And the one who is safe from this is occupied with his Lord and has drawn near to Him in his journey. How then can this (repentant) one catch up? This and similar arguments are what this group cited for their view.

This question came up in the presence of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah. I heard him recount these three views in a bare, impartial manner. Then either I asked him, or he was asked, about which of them is correct. He said: The correct view is that among the repentant are those who return to a state like their former one, those who return to one more perfect than what they were, and those who return to one lower than what they were. If after repentance he is better than he was before the sin, more cautious, more diligent, more humble, more fearful, and more turning to Allah, then he returns to a higher state than before. If he was more perfect in these matters before the sin but did not return to them after repentance, then he returns to a lower state than he was in. If after repentance he is just like he was before the sin, he returns to his former station. This is the meaning of his words, may Allah be pleased with him.

I say: Here is an issue that this place is most fitting to clarify. It is this: when the penitent repents to Allah with sincere repentance, are those sins erased so that they are gone with neither a credit nor a debit to him, or, when they are erased, is a good deed recorded for him in place of each sin? This is among the matters on which people, among the exegetes (mufassirun) and others, have differed, in the past and in the present. Al-Zajjaj said: It is not that the good deed is put in place of the sin; rather, repentance is put in place of the sin, and the good deed comes along with repentance.

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: He makes their deeds, in place of their former sins, into obedience, and this becomes a cause for Allah's mercy toward them. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Ibn Zayd, and al-Hasan. He refuted the one who said it refers to the Day of Resurrection. He said: A hadith has come in Sahih Muslim through the route of Abu Dharr which indicates that on the Day of Resurrection Allah, Glorified is He, will make good deeds in place of the sins of those among the monotheists whom He wills to forgive. It was also mentioned by al-Tirmidhi and al-Tabari. This is the interpretation of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib of this verse. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This is the meaning of the generosity of pardon. This is the end of his words.

I say: The hadith will come, God willing, with its full wording and discussion of it. Al-Mahdawi said: The meaning of this view was also narrated from Salman al-Farisi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others.

Al-Tha'labi said: Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Jurayj, al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [Al-Furqan: 70]: Allah will replace the ugly deeds they did in shirk with the beautiful deeds of Islam. He will replace shirk with faith, the killing of believers with the killing of polytheists, and fornication with chastity and marriage. Others said: it means Allah will replace the sins they committed while in Islam with good deeds on the Day of Resurrection.

The root of the two views is whether this replacement occurs in this world or on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever says it occurs in this world says it is the replacement of ugly deeds and corrupt intentions with their opposites, which are good deeds, and this is a true replacement. Those who supported this view argued that a sin does not turn into a good deed; rather, its utmost outcome is that it is erased, expiated, and its effect removed. But that it turns into a good deed, no. For it was never an act of obedience. It was rather something hateful and disliked by the Lord, so how could it turn into something beloved and pleasing?

They said: Moreover, what the Qur'an indicates is only the expiation of sins and the forgiveness of wrongs, as in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins and expiate from us our evil deeds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 193], and His saying: ﴿And He pardons evil deeds﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 15], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ [Al-Zumar: 53]. The Qur'an is full of such things.

In the Sahih from the hadith of Qatadah, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, who said: A man said to Ibn 'Umar: How did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ speak about the private conference (with Allah)? He said: I heard him say: "The believer will be brought near to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection until He places His hand (kanf) upon him, then He will make him acknowledge his sins. He will say: Do you recognize (this)? He will say: My Lord, I recognize it. He will say: I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you. Then he will be given the record of his good deeds. As for the disbelievers and the hypocrites, they will be called out before the witnesses: These are the ones who lied against Allah, Mighty and Majestic." This hadith, agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, which contains the honor shown to this servant, includes only the concealment of his sins for him in this world and their forgiveness for him on the Day of Resurrection. It does not say: "And I gave you a good deed for every sin."

This shows that the ultimate end of sins is their forgiveness and Allah's overlooking them. Allah has said about the truthful: ﴿That Allah may expiate from them the worst of what they did and reward them their best deeds for what they used to do﴾ [Al-Zumar: 35]. These are the best of creation, and He has informed that He expiates their evil deeds and rewards them according to the best of what they do. The best of what they did is good deeds, not evil ones. This shows that the reward with the best is given only for good deeds alone. As for sins, it is sufficient that they are nullified and their effect is voided.

They said: Moreover, if the sins themselves were turned into good deeds in the case of the penitent, he would be in a better state than one who committed no sins at all, and would have more good deeds than him. For when he sinned, he shared in the good deeds he did and was distinguished from him by those sins. Then, if the sins turned into good deeds for him, they would outweigh his. How can the one with sins be weightier than the one who has no sins?

They said: Moreover, just as when a servant does good deeds and then does something that nullifies them, those deeds do not turn into bad deeds for which he is punished. Rather, their effect is voided, and they are neither to his credit nor to his debit, and his punishment is that his reward for them is not recorded. Likewise, whoever commits sins and then repents from them, those sins do not turn into good deeds.

If you say: Likewise, the penitent's reward is that the punishment for his sins is not recorded, we do not dispute this with you. But this is not the meaning of a good deed, for a good deed entails a positive reward.

The other group, who said that it is the literal replacement of the evil deed with a good deed on the Day of Resurrection, argued: The true meaning of replacement is establishing a good deed in place of an evil deed.

This only applies to an actual evil deed, which has been done and has occurred. So when it is replaced with a good deed, it means that it has been erased and a good deed has been established in its place. They said: This is why He, Exalted, said: ﴿Their evil deeds into good deeds﴾ [Al-Furqan: 70]. He attributed the evil deeds to them because they performed and earned them, and He made the good deeds indefinite and did not attribute them to them, because they are not of their making or earning, but are purely the bounty and generosity of Allah.

They said: Moreover, the replacement in the verse is an act of Allah, not of them. He informed that He Himself replaces their evil deeds with good deeds. If what you mentioned were meant, He would have attributed the replacement to them, for they are the ones who replace their evil deeds with good deeds. Actions are attributed to their doer and earner, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿But those who did wrong substituted a word other than that which had been said to them﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 59]. As for what is not from the doer, He attributes its replacement to Himself, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens﴾ [Saba': 16]. Since He, Glorified is He, informed that He is the one who replaces their evil deeds with good deeds, this shows that it is something He Himself does to their evil deeds, not something they did of their own accord, even though its cause comes from them, namely repentance, faith, and righteous deeds.

They said: This is indicated by what Muslim narrated in his Sahih, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I know the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise, and the last of the people of Hellfire to leave it: a man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: Present to him his minor sins and withhold from him his major ones. His minor sins will be presented to him, and it will be said: On such and such a day you did such and such, and on such and such a day you did such and such? He will say: Yes, and he cannot deny it, while he is apprehensive about his major sins being presented to him. It will be said to him: For you, in place of every evil deed, there is a good deed. He will say: My Lord, I did things that I do not see here." Abu Dharr said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh until his back teeth showed.

Al-Imam Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said: Present to him his minor sins. So they will be presented to him, and his major sins will be hidden from him. It will be said: On such and such a day you did such and such? He will acknowledge it and not deny it, while he is apprehensive about the major sins. It will be said: Give him, in place of every evil deed he did, a good deed. He will say: Indeed, I have sins that I do not see." Abu Dharr said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laugh until his back teeth showed.

They said: Moreover, Abu Hafs al-Mustamli narrated from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Razmah, who said: al-Fadl ibn Musa al-Qati'i narrated to us, from Abu al-'Anbas, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Certainly some people will wish that they had committed more evil deeds." It was asked: Who are they? He said: "Those whose evil deeds Allah replaced with good deeds."

They said: These are truly the Abdal (substitutes), for they were only called Abdal because they replaced their evil deeds with good deeds. So Allah replaced the evil deeds they did with good deeds. They said: Moreover, recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Just as they replaced their evil deeds with good deeds, Allah replaced them in the records of the angels with good deeds as a recompense in kind.

The first group said: How can you argue with the hadith of Abu Dharr for the soundness of your view, when it is explicit that this person whose evil deeds were replaced with good deeds was punished for them in the Fire until he was the last of its people to leave it? So he was punished for his evil deeds, and their effect was removed by the punishment, and then a good deed was substituted for each one. This is a case different from what we are discussing, for the discussion concerns the penitent from sins, not someone who died persisting in them without repentance. How can one be compared with the other?

As for the hadith of Imam Ahmad, it is the very same hadith in chain and text, except that it is abridged.

As for the hadith of Abu Hurairah, a hadith like it is not established. Who is Abu al-'Anbas, and who is his father, that their solitary transmission of such a weighty matter should be accepted? And how could such a hadith be authentically from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, given his intense eagerness to make people averse to evil deeds, to condemn and disparage their doers, and to inform that they diminish good deeds and oppose them? How could it be authentic from him ﷺ that he says: "Certainly some people will wish that they had committed more of them"? Furthermore, how would a person wish to increase them, given their evil consequence and their bad end? One only wishes to increase acts of obedience. In al-Tirmidhi, there is a hadith traced to the Prophet ﷺ: "Certainly some people will wish on the Day of Resurrection that their skins had been cut with scissors, because of what they see of the reward of the people of trials."

In this, there is a wish for trials on the Day of Resurrection because of the increased reward of those who endured them, and this is a wish for good deeds. As for wishing for good deeds, there is no doubt about it. But as for wishing for evil deeds, how could a servant wish that he had committed more evil deeds? This is an impossible notion. Rather, the one who does evil wishes that he had not done evil. As for wishing that he had increased his evil, no!

They said: As for what you mentioned, that the replacement is the establishment of a good deed in place of an evil deed, that is correct. Likewise we say: the good deed done has taken the place of the evil deed which, were it not for the good deed, would have occupied its place. They said: As for your argument from attributing the evil deeds to them, this implies that they are the actual evil deeds that occurred. And the indefiniteness of the good deeds implies that they are good deeds from Allah's bounty. This is true without doubt. But from where does it follow that Allah's bounty must be concurrent with their earning of them by His bounty? They said: As for your statement that the replacement is attributed to Allah, not to them, which implies that He is the one who replaced them from the records, and not that they themselves replaced the deeds with their opposites, there is no proof for you in this. For Allah is the creator of the actions of His servants. He is the one who replaces the evil deeds with good deeds in creation and bringing into being, and they are the ones who replace them in action and earning.

They said: As for your argument that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, just as they replaced their evil deeds with good ones, so God replaces them in the records of deeds, this is true, and we say the same: the evil deeds which were prepared and set to appear in the records are replaced by good deeds which take their place.

This is the furthest point the steps of both groups reach, and the target of the gaze of both parties. And as for you, O fair-minded one, the judgment between them is yours, for each of them has presented his argument and established his proof, and the truth does not exceed them or go beyond them. So may God guide the one who is helped to guidance and attains thereby the rank of those who call to God and stand firm in explaining His proofs and His religion, or who excuses a seeker traveling alone on the road of his quest, whose hope of a companion on the way has been cut off, so that his greatest wish is that he be left to continue his journey and that his path not be cut off.

Whoever is shown such knowledge and does not aspire to it has been content with the lowly, and has obtained the bargain of the defrauded. And whoever aspires to it and wishes that no opponent oppose him and no obstructer confront him has set for himself an impossibility. And if he is patient with its hardships and its severity, then by God he has the clear victory and the abundant portion. And my success is only by God; upon Him I rely and to Him I turn in repentance.

So the correct position on this question, God willing, is to say: There is no doubt that the sin itself does not turn into a good deed, and a good deed is only an existential matter that calls for a reward. For this reason, the one who abandons what is forbidden is rewarded only for restraining his soul and withholding it from committing what is forbidden, and that restraint and withholding is an existential matter, and it is the object of the reward.

As for the one whose mind never brought up the sin at all and who never entertained it, how could he be rewarded for abandoning it? If such a person were rewarded for abandoning this sin, he would be rewarded for abandoning the sins of the whole world which never occurred to his mind, and that would exceed his good deeds without number, for abandonment accompanies him, and what is abandoned is not limited or bounded. Would he be rewarded for all of that? This is not even conceivable.

And if a good deed must be an existential matter, then the penitent from the sins he committed has accompanied each of them with regret for it, restraint of his soul from it, and resolve to never return to it. These are good deeds without doubt, and repentance has erased the trace of the sin and left behind this regret and resolve, and this is a good deed which has replaced that evil deed with a good deed.

This is the meaning of the saying of some exegetes: "He makes the repentance take the place of the evil deed, and the good deed is with the repentance."

So if every evil deed of his has been repented of, then his repentance from it is a good deed which has taken its place. This is the meaning of substitution, not that the evil deed itself turns into a good deed.

Some exegetes said regarding this verse: "He gives them, through regret for every evil they committed, a good deed." According to this, by God's praise the difficulty has gone away, the correct view has become clear, and it has become evident that each of the two groups did not depart from the requirement of knowledge and proof.

As for the hadith of Abu Dhar, although the substitution in it concerns the persistent sinner who was punished for his evil deeds, it indicates by way of a stronger inference that substitution occurs for the penitent who has ceased and regrets his evil deeds. For the sins for which the persistent one was punished, when their trace was removed by the punishment, remained as though they had never been. So God gives him, in place of each of them, a good deed, because what befell him on the Day of Resurrection of excessive regret for them, together with the punishment, necessitated the removal of their trace and their substitution with good deeds. For regret was not at a time when it would benefit him, so when he was punished for them and their trace was removed, God replaced them for him with good deeds.

So the removal of their trace through sincere repentance is greater than the removal of their trace through punishment. Therefore, if they are replaced with good deeds after their removal through punishment, then their replacement with good deeds after their removal through repentance is more fitting and more deserving. And the effect of repentance in this erasure and substitution is stronger than the effect of punishment, because repentance is a voluntary act which the servant performs willingly, out of love for God and fear of Him.

As for punishment, its expiation is of the same kind as the expiation through calamities that befall him without his choice, rather by the act of God. And there is no doubt that the effect of voluntary acts which God loves and is pleased with in erasing sins is greater than the effect of calamities that reach him without his choice.

Amr ibn Murrah said about ﴿and those who do not witness falsehood﴾: they do not collude with the people of shirk in their shirk, and they do not mingle with them. Al-Dahhak said something similar.

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "Here, *al-zur* (falsehood) means singing (*al-ghina'*)." Layth reported the same from Mujahid.

Al-Kalbi said: they do not attend gatherings of falsehood.

In the language, *al-laghw* is everything that is discarded and cast aside. The meaning is that they do not attend gatherings of falsehood, and when they pass by anything discarded, whether a word or a deed, they are too dignified to stop at it or incline toward it.

This includes the festivals of the polytheists, as the early scholars (*al-salaf*) explained it, singing (*al-ghina'*), and all kinds of falsehood.

Al-Zajjaj said: "They do not sit with the people of sins, nor do they collude with them in them. They pass by like noble people who do not approve of vain talk, because they honor themselves too much to enter into it or to mix with its people."

It is related that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, passed by a frivolous amusement and turned away from it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Ibn Mas'ud has become truly noble."

Allah the Exalted has also praised those who turn away from vain talk when they hear it, saying: ﴿When they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say: "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds."﴾ [al-Qasas: 55]

Although the occasion of this verse's revelation was specific, its meaning is general. It covers everyone who hears vain talk and turns away from it, saying to his companions, with his tongue or in his heart: "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds."

Consider how He said ﴿they do not witness falsehood﴾ and did not say "they do not witness *in* falsehood," because *shahada* here means "to attend." He praised them for not attending gatherings of falsehood. So how much more would it be for them to speak it or do it?

Singing is among the greatest of falsehoods.

The word *zur* is applied to false speech, to false action, and to the thing itself, as in the report of Mu'awiyah when he took a strand of hair used for extensions and said: "This is *zur*."

So *zur* refers to speech, action, and the object.

The root of the word is inclination. From it comes *zur* (with a fatha), and from it: "I visited (*zurtu*) so-and-so," meaning I inclined toward him and turned to him. So *zur* is a turning away from the established truth toward falsehood that has no reality, in speech and in deed.

(Section)

On His saying ﴿and when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity﴾:

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: "It is singing." Al-Hasan or someone else said: "They honor their souls from hearing it."

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Singing makes hypocrisy (*nifaq*) grow in the heart as water makes herbs grow." This is the speech of one who knows the effect of singing and its fruit. Whoever becomes accustomed to it, his heart becomes hypocritical while he does not perceive it. If he knew the reality of hypocrisy and its ultimate end, he would see it in his heart. Love of singing and love of the Qur'an never gather in a servant's heart without one of them driving out the other. Both we and others have witnessed how heavy the Qur'an is for the people of singing and its listening, their impatience with it, their shouting at the reciter when he prolongs the recitation, and their hearts' failure to benefit from what he recites. They are not moved, they do not feel delight, and no yearning for seeking is stirred in them. But when the "Qur'an of Satan" comes, they say "There is no god but Allah," and how their voices grow humble, their movements grow still, their hearts become calm and at rest, weeping and ecstasy occur, both outward and inward movement arises, they become generous with money and clothing, they delight in staying up late, and they wish the night would last longer. If this is not hypocrisy, then it is at least its core and foundation.

The Book is recited, and they lower their gaze, not out of fear,
but it is the lowering of one who is heedless and frivolous.

Singing comes, and they dance like flies,
by Allah, they did not dance for the sake of Allah.

A tambourine, a flute, and the sound of a witness (*shahid*),
so when do you witness worship mixed with amusements?

The Book became heavy for them when they saw
it binding them with commands and prohibitions.

But singing became light for them when they saw
its release into amusement without prohibitions.

O party whom the religion of Muhammad has not harmed
or wronged, except that it has become tiresome to them!

They heard from it thunder and lightning, when it contained
warning and fear through the performance of prohibitions.

They saw it as the greatest severer of the soul from
its desires, alas for it, the one who reaches its end!

Listening came to agree with its aims,
so for its sake he became great in rank tomorrow.

Where is the one who helps desire against the one who cuts
its causes, in the sight of the ignorant and heedless?

If it is not the wine of bodies, then it is
the wine of minds, similar and equal to it.

So look at the intoxicated one at his drink,
and look at the intoxicated one at his amusement.

And look at the one who tears his garments
after the tearing of the heedless heart.

So judge which of the two wines deserves more
the prohibition and the sin in the sight of Allah.

And how can the listening that a servant hears by his nature and desire be more beneficial to him than the listening that he hears through Allah, for Allah, and from Allah?

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 25, verse 73:

Muqatil said: "When they are admonished with the Qur'an, they do not fall upon it as deaf people who do not hear it, or blind people who do not see it. Rather, they hear and they see, and they are certain of it."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They were not deaf and blind toward it; rather, they were fearful and humbled."

al-Kalbi said: "They fall upon it, hearing and seeing."

al-Farra' said: "When the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not remain seated in their former state, as if they had not heard it. This is the meaning of 'falling down' (kharur). The Arabs say qa'ada yashtamuni (he sat and insulted me), just as you say qama yashtamuni (he stood and insulted me) and aqbala yashtamuni (he came and insulted me)."

The meaning according to what has been mentioned is: they did not become deaf and blind in its presence.

al-Zajjaj said: "The meaning is: when it is recited to them, they fall down prostrating and weeping, hearing and seeing as they were commanded."

Ibn Qutayba said: "That is, they did not neglect it, as if they were deaf who did not hear it or blind who did not see it."

I say: Here there are two matters. The first is the mention of falling down (kharur) and the application of negation to it. The second is whether it is the falling of the heart or the falling of the body in prostration?

Does the meaning become: their falling was not from deafness and blindness, so for them there is a falling upon it with the heart, in submission, or with the body, in prostration?

Or is there no falling, and it is an expression used for sitting?

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 25, verse 74:

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us: Hazm narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan, and Kathir ibn Ziyad asked him about the words of the Exalted: ﴿Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring the delight of our eyes﴾.

He said: "O Abu Sa'id, what is this delight of the eyes? Is it in this world or in the Hereafter?"

He said: "No, by Allah, it is in this world."

He said: "And what is it?"

He said: "By Allah, it is that Allah shows the servant, from his wife, his brother, his close relative, obedience to Allah. No, by Allah, nothing is more beloved to the believing man than to see a son, a father, a close relative, or a brother obedient to Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And make us leaders for the God-fearing﴾.

"Imam" here means a model to be followed, and it can be used for the singular and the plural, like ummah (community) and uswah (example).

It has been said that it is the plural of amim, like sahib (companion) and sihab (companions), rajil (man on foot) and rijal (men), tajir (merchant) and tujjar (merchants).

It has also been said that it is a verbal noun (masdar) like qital (fighting) and dirab (striking), meaning "possessors of an imam."

The correct view is the first, for every one of the God-fearing is obliged to be followed by them, piety is obligatory, following them is obligatory, and opposing them in what they have ruled is opposition to following them.

(Section)

Allah, glorified is He, has praised His believing servants who ask Him to make them leaders who are guided by. He said, describing His servants: ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring the delight of our eyes, and make us leaders for the God-fearing."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: "They are guided by us in good." Abu Salih said: "They are followed for our guidance."

Makhul said: "Leaders in piety, whom the God-fearing follow."

Mujahid said: "Make us those who follow the God-fearing and take them as models." This interpretation was difficult for those who did not know the extent of the understanding and depth of knowledge of the early generations (al-salaf). He said that the verse on this view must be of the type of inversion (al-maqlub), meaning "and make the God-fearing leaders for us." But God forbid that anything be inverted from its proper form. This is part of Mujahid's complete understanding, may Allah have mercy on him, for a man does not become a leader for the God-fearing until he follows the God-fearing. Mujahid drew attention to this way by which they attain this goal, which is their following of the God-fearing early generations before them, so that Allah makes them leaders for the God-fearing after them. This is among the finest understanding of the Qur'an and its most subtle, and it is not at all a case of inversion. Whoever follows the People of the Sunnah before him, those after him and those with him will follow him.

He, glorified is He, used the singular word ﴿imaman﴾ and did not say "a'immah" (leaders). It has been said that imam in the verse is the plural of amm, like sahib and sihab; this is the view of al-Akhfash, but it is weak, and it is not from the well-known, commonly used language by which the speech of Allah should be explained.

Others said that imam here is a verbal noun, not a noun of agent, as one says amma imaman like sama siyaman and qama qiyaman, meaning "make us possessors of an imam." This is weaker than the previous view.

al-Farra' said: He said ﴿imaman﴾ and did not say a'immah, in the manner of His saying ﴿Indeed, we are a messenger of the Lord of the worlds﴾, and He did not say rusulan. It is the singular used to mean the plural, following the words of the poet:

(O my blamers, do not return my reproach, for the blamers are not my commanders.)

meaning: they are not my commanders (plural).

This is the best of the views, but it needs further explanation: the God-fearing are all upon one path, their object of worship is one, they follow one book, one prophet, and are servants of one Lord. Their religion is one, their prophet is one, their book is one, and their object of worship is one. So they are, as it were, one imam for those after them, unlike the differing imams whose paths, methods and creeds have diverged. Following is only by what they are upon, and that is one thing, and it is the imam in reality.

He, glorified is He, has informed that this leadership is attained only through patience and certainty, when He said: ﴿And We made among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs﴾.

Through patience and certainty, leadership in religion is attained.

It has been said: through patience over the world.

It has been said: through patience over trials.

It has been said: through patience over what is forbidden. The correct view is that it is through patience over all of that: patience in performing Allah's obligations, patience in refraining from His prohibitions, and patience in His decrees.

He, glorified is He, combined patience and certainty, for they are the happiness of the servant, and losing them causes him to lose his happiness. The heart is visited by the passing desires that oppose the command of Allah and by the passing doubts that oppose His report. Through patience one repels desires, and through certainty one repels doubts. Desire and doubt are both opposed to religion in every respect, so none is saved from the punishment of Allah except one who repels his desires by patience and his doubts by certainty.

[Section: The difference between love of leadership and love of command for the call to Allah]

The difference between love of leadership (ri'asah) and love of command (imarah) for calling to Allah is the difference between exalting the command of Allah and advising Him, and exalting the self and striving for its share. The sincere advisor to Allah is one who exalts Him and loves Him, and loves that his Lord be obeyed, not disobeyed, that His word be supreme, that religion be entirely for Allah, and that the servants be complying with His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. He has advised Allah in His worship and advised His creation in calling to Allah. This is leadership in religion. Indeed, his Lord is asked to make him an imam for the God-fearing, whom the God-fearing follow, just as he himself followed the God-fearing. If this servant who calls to Allah loves that he be esteemed in their eyes, awe-inspiring in their hearts, beloved to them, and obeyed among them, so that they follow him and trace the footsteps of the Messenger through him, this does not harm him; rather he is praised for it, because he is a caller to Allah who loves to be obeyed, worshipped and affirmed in His oneness. He loves what helps him in that and leads to it. For this reason He, glorified, mentioned His servants whom He chose for Himself and praised in His revelation, and gave them the best reward on the day of meeting Him. He mentioned them by their best deeds and qualities, then said: ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring the delight of our eyes, and make us leaders for the God-fearing."﴾

They asked Him to delight their eyes through the obedience of their spouses and offspring to Him, glorified is He, and to gladden their hearts through the God-fearing following them in obedience and servitude to Him. The leader and the follower cooperate in obedience. They only asked for what would help them and the God-fearing to His good pleasure and obedience, which is calling to Allah through leadership in religion, which Allah has honoured with patience and certainty, as He said: ﴿And We made among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs﴾.

Their request that He make them leaders for the God-fearing is a request that He guide them, grant them success, and bestow upon them beneficial knowledge and righteous deeds, outwardly and inwardly, without which leadership is not complete.

Consider how, in these verses, He attributed them to His name al-Rahman, exalted is His majesty, so that His creation may know that they attained this only through the grace of His mercy and the pure bounty of His favour.

Consider how, in this surah, He made their reward the lofty chambers (al-ghurfah), which are the high dwellings in Paradise, since leadership in religion is among the lofty ranks, indeed the highest rank a servant can be given in religion, so its reward is the lofty chamber in Paradise.

This is in contrast to the seeking of leadership, for its seekers strive to obtain it so that they may reach their aims of elevation on earth, hearts being enslaved to them and inclining towards them, and people helping them in all their aims, while they are high above them and dominate them. This pursuit entails corruptions known only to Allah: rebellion, envy, tyranny, malice, injustice, sedition, and zeal for the self rather than for the right of Allah, exalting one whom Allah has belittled, and despising one whom Allah has honoured.

Worldly leadership is not complete without this, it is not attained except with this and with its multiples of corruptions, and leaders are blind to this.

When the veil is lifted, their corruption will be made clear to them, especially when they are gathered in the form of ants, trampled by the people of the gathering with their feet, in humiliation, debasement and diminishment, just as they diminished the command of Allah and despised His servants.

The Ghurfah (the lofty chamber) is a genus, like Jannah (Paradise). Reflect on how their reward was given for these statements that express submission, humbleness and lowliness before Allah: the Ghurfah, the greeting (al-tahiyyah) and peace, in return for their patience over the bad speech of the ignorant towards them. Thus they were given, in exchange, the peace of Allah and His angels.

(Section)

Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn said: "al-Ghurfah" is Paradise. "Bima sabaru" (for what they endured with patience) he said: this refers to poverty in this world.

It is also narrated that Anas reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "O Allah, let me live as a poor man, let me die as a poor man, and resurrect me in the company of the poor on the Day of Resurrection."

Then Aishah said: "And why, O Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "They will enter Paradise before the rich by forty autumns. O Aishah, do not turn away a poor man even with half a date. O Aishah, love the poor and bring them near, for Allah will bring you near on the Day of Resurrection."

I say: There is no proof for him in either of the two arguments.

As for the verse, the patience in it encompasses the patience of the thankful in obeying Allah, his patience in refraining from what is forbidden, his patience in calamity, and the patience of one tested with poverty or other things in his trial. Even if its intended meaning were patience in poverty alone, its superiority would not indicate superiority over gratitude, for the Qur'an, just as it indicates the reward of the patient, also indicates the reward of the grateful, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We will reward the grateful﴾ and ﴿And Allah will reward the grateful﴾.

Indeed, He has informed that His pleasure lies in gratitude, and His pleasure is greater than His reward with the gardens and what is in them. When Allah rewards the patient with the Ghurfah for what they endured, that does not indicate that He does not reward the grateful with the Ghurfah for what they showed gratitude for.

As for the hadith, there is no proof in it for two reasons:

The first: its chain cannot be used as evidence, for it is narrated through Muhammad ibn Thabit al-Kufi from al-Harith ibn al-Nu'man, and this al-Harith was not relied upon by the compilers of the Sahih; rather al-Bukhari said of him: "munkar al-hadith" (rejected in narration). For this reason al-Tirmidhi did not authenticate this hadith, nor did he grade it as good, nor did he remain silent about it, but he judged it to be gharib (strange).

The second answer: even if the hadith were authentic, it would not indicate their claim. The meekness (maskanah) that Allah loves from His servant is not poverty of wealth, but meekness of the heart, which is its brokenness, humility, submissiveness and lowliness before Allah. This meekness does not contradict wealth, nor is poverty a condition for it, for the heart's brokenness before Allah and its humility before His greatness, majesty, grandeur, names and attributes is superior and higher than the meekness of lacking wealth. Just as the patience of the wealthy person in refraining from Allah's disobedience voluntarily, by choice, out of fear of Allah and love for Him, is higher than the patience of the poor who is unable. Allah gave wealth and kingdom to a group of His prophets and messengers, and that did not remove them from meekness before Allah.

The most sound of the opinions regarding the verse is that its meaning is: "What would My Lord do with you were it not for your worship of Him?" For He, glorified is He, did not create you except to worship Him.
